record.title: Yacuiba–Salvador Mazza health-workers’ blockade with negotiated passage, July 2024
record.scope: Named international crossing and its immediate approach; no whole-country outline is inferred.
record.direction: Both directions were affected; the 22 July negotiated cohort travelled toward Argentina.
record.movement: Vehicles including international buses and freight, with documented temporary authorised passage
record.exceptions: The Defensoría documents a temporary 22 July pause for three international buses and 15 light vehicles. Broader and repeated exceptions are not fully reconstructed.
record.imposing_authority: Health workers demanding jobs and posts, supported by civic and trader groups
record.enforcement: Deliberate protest obstruction reported in the linked contemporary sources.
record.relationship: No matching event in the 726-parent B02 inventory or adjudicated R11–R14 additions; R16 West Africa is geographically disjoint. The same crossing does not make different dated protest campaigns duplicates.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no present border status inferred.
record.current_timing: Contested: Intermittent regime envelope; total closed days unknown
record.current_corrections: Contemporaneous evidence places the bridge blockade on 22 July; ANF later says 15 July. Both possibilities remain as contested onset bounds. A temporary passage on 22 July and general vehicle return after 28 July police clearance are documented, so neither six nor thirteen days is an established continuous all-traffic duration.

followup_reviews.Researcher: root and checkpoint_design, original half audits in separate GPT-6 Astra Pro contexts
followup_reviews.Separate challenger: rounds_protocol on baseline half; root on programme-addition half; same-model contexts, not independent human review
followup_reviews.Research finding: The July 2024 health-worker blockade and police clearance are supported within the observation period; retain the episode as included. Vehicles including buses and freight were affected, but the mediator documented a temporary passage toward Argentina for three buses and fifteen light vehicles. Both-direction general return on 28 July is separately reported. Retain contested 15–22 July onset bounds, observed 28 July endpoint, held=1 and withheld_intermittent_and_onset_conflict. The contemporary 22 July start conflicts with ANF’s later 15 July claim; the earlier protest campaign is not assumed to equal bridge closure. Exceptions preclude a continuous six- or thirteen-day calculation, so duration is null and complete flags remain zero. Policy and socioeconomic demands / Jobs, services and livelihoods remains supported by attributed demands for job security, funded posts and benefits. This is the protesters’ rationale rather than an inferred security justification for the police response. The primary mediating Defensoría account was freshly read. The conflicting ANF/El País and Visión 360 passages were reread from fingerprinted receipts. Fides-related reporting may share origins; participant claims and unviewed videos are not independently verified events. The phase remains unlocated at the international bridge. The known place name and a police-clearing account do not establish a surveyed barricade position or justify continuous closure animation.
